weeks.label: Week 9 - Head & Neck Anatomy, Masses & Infections

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Vagus in carotid sheath → superior laryngeal n.: external = motor to cricothyroid (injury → weak, tired voice / ↓ pitch); internal = sensory to superior larynx (cough reflex)
  • Recurrent laryngeal n. = motor to most laryngeal muscles → injury = hoarseness (unilateral), loss of voice (bilateral)
  • Right RLN loops the subclavian a.; left RLN loops the aortic arch

lectures.name: Integrative Upper Respiratory Tract and GI Tract Anatomy

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Nodules very common, more common in females; only 10-15% of palpable nodules malignant (Roth)
  • Work-up: TSH first → low TSH → RAI scan (hot nodule = benign, treat hyperthyroidism); normal/high → U/S (TI-RADS) → FNAB (Bethesda); thyroglobulin not recommended
  • Cancer risk: child, male, 1st-degree FHx, neck radiation; sx dysphagia, hoarseness, stridor, rapid growth; signs firm/fixed mass, suspicious LN
  • Papillary = most common thyroid ca (>85%), best prognosis
  • Post-thyroidectomy voice: RLN injury → unilateral hoarseness, bilateral airway obstruction; SLN injury → loss of pitch control

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Midline mass = thyroid thing 90% of the time; other 10%: LN, dermoid cyst, lymphatic malformation
  • Rule of 7s: 7 d infection · 7 wk-7 mo neoplasm · 7 y congenital
  • 80% rule: neoplastic → malignant → metastatic → H&N primary; + age rule → elderly lateral neck mass = cancer until proven otherwise
  • Reactive LN (reacts TO infection) vs suppurative lymphadenitis (node itself infected)
  • Stones: submandibular most common; 90% submandibular radiopaque, 90% parotid radiolucent; pain + swelling worse with meals
  • Acute sialadenitis: S. aureus, 25% bilateral; massage, warm compress, hydration, sialagogues, abx; no improvement in 3 d → assess for complications
  • Salivary tumours >80% parotid; smaller gland = greater chance of cancer (parotid 25%, SMG 50%, others 75%); risk = radiation, not smoking/EtOH except Warthin's
  • Salivary tumour red flags: facial nerve weakness, pain, skin changes, hard fixed mass, neck nodes
  • Every salivary gland mass → surgical excision, even if benign; cancers → post-op RT
  • SCC: HPV+ younger, healthier, non-smoker → better prognosis; HPV− older, smoker/drinker → poor
  • Leukoplakia (white) + erythroplasia (red) = premalignant
  • Tx by site: oral cavity surgery ± post-op RT · oropharynx RT + chemo · larynx RT (advanced → surgery + RT) · neck surgery ± RT

lectures.name: Infections of the Head and Neck
lectures.title: Infections of the Head and Neck

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Normal flora: skin S. aureus, GAS; mouth viridans strep + anaerobes (± yeast)
  • Not normal flora: otitis externa → Pseudomonas; bacterial sinusitis / OM → S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, S. aureus
  • Red flags: progressive sx, fever, ↓ neck ROM, trismus, prior abx; always consider the airway
  • Tonsillitis: peritonsillar swelling + uvula deviation → PTA → I&D; trismus + ↓ neck ROM → deep neck infection
  • Tonsillectomy (Paradise): 7 in 1 yr, 5/yr × 2 yr, 3/yr × 3 yr; also OSA, recurrent PTA, suspected malignancy
  • Epiglottitis (H. influenzae B, now uncommon): hot potato voice, tripod, drooling → secure airway, don't agitate
  • Diphtheria (C. diphtheriae): grey pharyngeal membrane + toxin myocarditis; unvaccinated
  • Deep neck space: oral flora → ceftriaxone + metronidazole; + vancomycin if MRSA colonized / PWID; + pip-tazo if immunocompromised / healthcare-associated; I&D ± steroids
  • Lemierre's = IJ septic thrombophlebitis, Fusobacterium necrophorum, after pharyngitis; CT with contrast; ceftriaxone + metronidazole; septic emboli
  • Rhinocerebral mucormycosis: DKA, immunocompromise, steroids, deferoxamine; rapid fever, sinus pain, headache → surgical debridement + liposomal amphotericin; very high mortality

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• LN >2 cm → not typical in children
  • Labs: CBC + diff, cat-scratch serology, tumour markers (VMA)
  • TGDC: 70% of congenital cysts, midline, elevates on tongue protrusion, enlarges/infected after URI
  • TGDC Tx: Sistrunk = cyst + central hyoid + tract up to foramen cecum; not during acute infection
  • 2nd branchial cleft = >90% of BC anomalies; lateral, usually right if unilateral; recurrent swelling with URI, discharge in lower neck
  • BC Tx: complete excision of sinus + tract; prior drainage/partial excision → recurrence 3% → 20% (don't drain)
  • Lymphatic malformation: present at birth, grows with child; surgery = Tx of choice

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• DDx stridor: croup most common, epiglottitis; less likely FB, VC paralysis
  • Croup: parainfluenza/RSV/influenza, 6 mo-3 y, subglottic; low fever, inspiratory stridor, barking "seal" cough, steeple sign
  • Croup Tx: hydration, cold humidification; mod-severe → nebulized epi + steroids; intubation rare
  • FB: 1-3 y, boys, vegetable matter 70-80%; 3 phases acute (choking) → asymptomatic → complication
  • FB Ix: inspiratory/expiratory CXR; most often right mainstem; rigid bronchoscopy if any 1 of Hx / exam / imaging positive
